instructions: Put 12 bamboo skewers in a dish of water to soak for at least 30 minutes.
In a small saucepan, stir together 1/4 cup water, the 1/4 cup sake, 1/2 cup mirin, 1/2 cup soy sauce and the 2 tsp brown sugar. Bring it to a boil over medium-high heat.

Turn the heat down to keep a gentle simmer and cook it for about 30 minutes, until it has reduced by half. That should be about 3/4 cup. It thickens as it cools, so take it off the heat while it's still pourable.
Meanwhile, put 1/2 lb of the ground chicken in a dry skillet over medium heat. Break it up with a spatula and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, until there's no pink left. Keep it pale. Don't let it brown.
Spread the cooked chicken on a plate and leave it for about 10 minutes, until it's completely cool.
Thinly slice 4 of the green onions.
In a large bowl, combine the cooled chicken, the remaining 1 lb raw chicken, the 1 1/2 tbsp miso and 1 1/2 tbsp of the sesame oil. Add the green onions.
Knead it with one hand, folding it over on itself, for about 2 minutes, until it turns pale and sticky. Divide it into 12 even portions.
Set an oven rack about 8 inches below the broiler and heat the broiler on high. Line a baking sheet with foil, set a wire rack on it and brush the rack with a little of the last 1/2 tbsp sesame oil.
Rub the rest of the sesame oil on your hands. Toss one portion back and forth between your palms to press out the air, then shape it into a 3 inch oval.
Push a skewer lengthwise into the oval and squeeze the meat around it into a firm, even log. Lay it on the rack. Shape the rest the same way, leaving room between them.
Sprinkle the 1/2 tsp coarse salt over the skewers. Wrap the bare ends of the skewers in small strips of foil so they don't burn.
Broil them for about 6 minutes, until browned in spots.

Flip each skewer and broil the other side for about 4 minutes. You're cooking them to 165°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check one there. No thermometer? Cut one open: it's done when there's no pink left and the juices run clear.
Brush the tops with the sauce and broil for 45 to 60 seconds, until the glaze bubbles. Watch them closely. The sugar burns fast.
Flip them, brush the other side and broil for 45 to 60 seconds.
Taste a little from the end of one. If it's flat, brush on a little more of the sauce.
Serve with the rest of the sauce and the shichimi togarashi on the side.
method_notes: All three versions make chicken meatballs and finish them in a sweet soy glaze of mirin, soy sauce, sake and sugar. Just One Cookbook (the lead) cooks a third of the chicken first so the mix holds on the skewer, kneads it with miso and sesame oil until sticky, broils the skewers and brushes on a sauce reduced by half; Food Faith Fitness binds the mix with panko and egg and grills it with a tare simmered with aromatics, and Japanese Cooking 101 pan fries small patties without skewers and pours a quick sauce over them. This one follows the lead for 1.5 lb of chicken, using the lead's full sauce, and leaves out the shiso leaves, which are hard to find; it uses 4 green onions instead.
